1. **Assessment & target sizing**: Inventory the 2 TB Postgres instance (extensions, version, custom types, sequences, large objects), size the target managed service (compute/storage/IOPS) accordingly, and confirm network path (VPN/peering) between on-prem and cloud.
2. **Build replication pipeline**: Provision the managed instance, match Postgres version/extensions, and set up logical replication (e.g., pglogical, native logical replication, or a CDC tool) or a physical replica for continuous sync from on-prem to cloud.
3. **Non-production dry run / rehearsal**: Clone a representative subset (or full copy) of production data into staging, execute the entire migration + cutover procedure end-to-end, and time each phase to validate the run fits within the 2-hour window.
4. **Refine runbook from rehearsal**: Document exact commands, timings, and failure points found in the dry run; adjust the plan and re-test any step that ran long or failed.
5. **Stakeholder communication (pre-migration)**: Notify all 4,000 users and internal stakeholders of the scheduled Sunday maintenance window, expected downtime, and fallback contact/status page, at least several days in advance with a reminder closer to the date.
6. **Pre-cutover full backup**: Immediately before the maintenance window, take a full verified backup (pg_basebackup or equivalent, plus WAL archive) of the production on-prem database — this must complete and be validated before any destructive/modifying step proceeds.
7. **Freeze writes and enter maintenance window**: Put the application into read-only/maintenance mode, stop write traffic to on-prem Postgres, and confirm no active write transactions remain.
8. **Final sync and promote target**: Let logical replication drain to zero lag, verify replica is caught up to the last on-prem transaction, then promote the managed cloud instance as the new primary (reset sequences, re-enable triggers/constraints as needed).
9. **Data integrity verification**: Compare row counts, table checksums (e.g., `pg_checksums`/`checksum` extension or hash aggregates per table), and key aggregate values between source backup and target; fail the cutover and roll back if discrepancies exceed tolerance.
10. **Cutover application traffic**: Repoint application connection strings/DNS to the managed cloud database, run smoke tests against critical read/write paths, then take the app out of maintenance mode.
11. **Rollback procedure (trigger if step 9 or 10 fails)**: Repoint application back to the original on-prem primary (still intact and untouched since backup), discard the partial cloud cutover, restore write access on-prem, and communicate the postponement to stakeholders; investigate before re-attempting.
12. **Post-cutover monitoring & stakeholder close-out**: Monitor performance/error rates on the cloud instance for 24–48 hours, keep the on-prem backup and replica available as a fallback for a defined retention period, then notify stakeholders that migration succeeded and close the maintenance window.

STEP COUNT: 12
